ayahs.1: Sad. By the Quran, rich in dhikr—conscious remembrance of Allah that warns, guides, and leaves no excuse.
ayahs.2: This is the truth—yet those who reject it are entrenched in arrogance and stubborn opposition.
ayahs.3: Consider how many communities We destroyed before them. They cried out when escape was already impossible.
ayahs.4: The pagans are astonished that a warner has come from among themselves. Those who reject the truth say, "This is a sorcerer, a total liar!"
ayahs.5: "Has he reduced all our gods to one Allah?" they ask—because tawhid, the oneness of Allah in worship and reliance, feels astonishing to hearts built on shirk.
ayahs.6: Their chiefs marched out saying, "Keep going, and stand firm with your gods. This is clearly a scheme for power."
ayahs.7: "We never heard this in the earlier faith. This is nothing but a fabrication."
ayahs.8: "Was the Reminder revealed only to him out of all of us?" In truth they doubt My Reminder because they have not yet tasted My punishment.
ayahs.9: Or do they possess the treasuries of your Lord's mercy—the Rahman, whose mercy in this life extends over all creation, the Almighty, the Giver of every bounty?
ayahs.10: Or does the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and everything between belong to them? Let them climb their way to heaven, if their claim is true.
ayahs.11: This is only another doomed force heading toward defeat.
ayahs.12: Before them the people of Nuh denied the truth, as did 'Ad, Pharaoh of the mighty structures,
ayahs.13: Thamud, the people of Lut, and the dwellers of the Forest—these were all hostile forces united in rejection.
ayahs.14: Each community rejected its messenger, so My punishment was fully justified.
ayahs.15: These pagans await nothing but a single Blast that cannot be stopped or postponed.
ayahs.16: They mockingly say, "Our Lord, hasten our share of punishment before the Day of Reckoning!"
ayahs.17: Be patient with what they say, O Prophet. Remember Our servant Dawud, a man of strength who constantly turned back to Allah.
ayahs.18: We subjected the mountains to glorify Allah with him at evening and after sunrise.
ayahs.19: And the birds gathered in flocks, all echoing his praise—creation joining the worship of its Rabb.
ayahs.20: We strengthened his kingship and gave him wisdom and sound judgment.
ayahs.21: Has the story of the two disputants who climbed over Dawud's sanctuary wall reached you?
ayahs.22: When they burst in upon him, he was startled. They said, "Do not fear—we are two in a dispute. One of us has wronged the other. Judge between us with truth, do not exceed it, and guide us to the right way."
ayahs.23: "This is my brother. He has ninety-nine sheep while I have only one. Still he demanded I give mine to him, overwhelming me with his argument."
ayahs.24: Dawud ruled: "He has wronged you by demanding your sheep be added to his. Many partners wrong one another—except those who believe and do good, and how few they are!" Then he realized We had tested him. He asked his Lord's forgiveness, fell in prostration, and turned in repentance.
ayahs.25: We forgave him that. He will have closeness to Us and an honourable destination.
ayahs.26: We told him: "O Dawud, We have made you an authority in the land. Judge between people with truth. Do not follow your nafs—the inner self that pulls toward desire—or it will lead you astray from Allah's way. Those who stray from Allah's way face severe punishment for neglecting the Day of Reckoning."
ayahs.27: We did not create the heavens and the earth and everything between without purpose, as those who reject the truth assume. Woe to them because of the Fire.
ayahs.28: Should We treat those who believe and do good like those who spread corruption in the land? Should We treat the righteous like the wicked?
ayahs.29: This is a blessed Book We revealed to you so they may contemplate its ayahs—signs and verses—and so people of reason may take heed.
ayahs.30: We granted Dawud Sulayman—what an excellent servant! He too constantly turned back to Allah.
ayahs.31: When well-trained, swift horses were paraded before him in the evening,
ayahs.32: he said, "I love these fine things for the sake of remembering Allah"—until they passed out of sight.
ayahs.33: He ordered, "Bring them back to me!" Then he began stroking their legs and necks.
ayahs.34: We tested Sulayman by placing a deformed body on his throne. Then he turned back to Allah in repentance.
ayahs.35: He prayed, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom no one after me will match. You are the Giver of every bounty."
ayahs.36: We subjected the wind to him, blowing gently at his command wherever he wished.
ayahs.37: And We subjected every builder and diver among the jinn,
ayahs.38: and others bound together in chains.
ayahs.39: Allah said: "This is Our gift—give or withhold as you wish, without being called to account."
ayahs.40: He too will have closeness to Us and an honourable destination.
ayahs.41: Remember Our servant Ayyub, when he cried to his Lord: "Satan has afflicted me with distress and suffering."
ayahs.42: We said: "Strike the ground with your foot—here is cool water for washing and drinking."
ayahs.43: We restored his family to him, twice as many, as mercy from Us and a lesson for people of reason.
ayahs.44: We told him: "Take a bundle of grass in your hand and strike with it without breaking your oath." We found him patient—what an excellent servant! He constantly turned back to Allah.
ayahs.45: Remember Our servants Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Ya'qub—men of strength and insight.
ayahs.46: We chose them for the honour of proclaiming the Akhirah—the everlasting life after death.
ayahs.47: In Our sight they are truly among the chosen and the finest.
ayahs.48: Remember Isma'il, Alyasa', and Dhul-Kifl—all among the best.
ayahs.49: This is a reminder. The righteous will certainly have an honourable destination:
ayahs.50: the Gardens of Eternity, whose gates will be open for them.
ayahs.51: There they will recline, calling for abundant fruit and drink.
ayahs.52: With them will be companions of modest gaze and equal age.
ayahs.53: This is what you are promised for the Day of Reckoning.
ayahs.54: This is Our provision that will never end.
ayahs.55: That is for the righteous. The transgressors will have the worst destination:
ayahs.56: Hell, where they will burn—what an evil place to rest.
ayahs.57: Let them taste boiling water and oozing pus,
ayahs.58: and other torments of the same kind.
ayahs.59: The misleaders will say to one another, "Here is a crowd being thrown in with us. They are not welcome—they too will burn in the Fire."
ayahs.60: The followers will answer, "No—you are not welcome! You brought this upon us. What an evil place to settle!"
ayahs.61: They will add, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, double their punishment in the Fire."
ayahs.62: The tyrants will ask, "Why do we not see those we considered lowly among us?"
ayahs.63: Were we wrong to mock them in the dunya—this temporary worldly life—or do our eyes simply fail to see them here?
ayahs.64: This dispute among the people of the Fire will certainly take place.
ayahs.65: Say: "I am only a warner. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah—the One, the Supreme."
ayahs.66: He is the Rabb of the heavens and the earth and everything between—the Almighty, ever-forgiving.
ayahs.68: from which you pagans are turning away."
ayahs.69: Say: "I had no knowledge of the highest assembly in heaven when they disputed over Adam.
ayahs.70: What is revealed to me is only that I am sent with a clear warning."
ayahs.71: Remember when your Lord said to the angels: "I am creating a human being from clay.
ayahs.72: When I have fashioned him and breathed into him a spirit of My creation, fall down in prostration to him."
ayahs.74: except Iblis, who acted arrogantly and became among the unfaithful.
ayahs.75: Allah asked: "O Iblis, what stopped you from prostrating to what I created with My own hands? Did you become proud, or were you always arrogant?"
ayahs.76: He replied: "I am better than he is. You created me from fire and him from clay."
ayahs.77: Allah commanded: "Then get out of Paradise—you are cursed.
ayahs.78: My condemnation is upon you until the Day of Judgment."
ayahs.79: Satan appealed: "My Lord, then delay my end until the Day they are resurrected."
ayahs.82: Satan vowed: "By Your glory, I will mislead them all,
ayahs.83: except Your chosen servants among them."
ayahs.84: Allah concluded: "The truth is—and I only speak the truth—
ayahs.85: I will fill Hell with you and whoever follows you from among them, all together."
ayahs.86: Say: "I do not ask you for any reward for this Quran, nor do I pretend to be what I am not.
ayahs.87: It is only a reminder to all the worlds.
ayahs.88: And you will certainly know its truth before long."
